stage_2_story.text_en:
On Wednesday morning, Avi woke up with a bad cough and a sore throat. He decided not to call a doctor straight away and instead went to the pharmacy to ask for advice.

When he arrived, the pharmacist greeted him and listened carefully as Avi described his symptoms. The pharmacist suggested an over-the-counter syrup for the cough — no prescription needed. He also recommended a throat spray and told Avi to take one tablet of paracetamol every six hours if he had a temperature.

Avi picked up the medicines and asked about the dosage for the syrup. The pharmacist said two teaspoons three times a day, always after eating. He also warned Avi about one of the side effects: the syrup might make him feel a little drowsy, so he should avoid driving.

Avi noticed the cough syrup had a generic label and asked if it worked as well as the branded version. The pharmacist explained it was exactly the same medicine, just a cheaper version.

Before leaving, Avi also asked for a refill of his father's heart medication. He handed over the prescription and the pharmacist processed it quickly. Avi checked the expiry dates on all the boxes and paid at the counter. He thanked the pharmacist and went home to rest.
